newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin confident before surgery - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin confident before surgery - spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, in a statement released before the start of Tuesday's operation on his heart, said he was sure surgery would go well and reassured Russians there would be no power vacuum.

Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference that Yeltsin had handed power over to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin before the operation started. "The country will not be without a leader for a minute," Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin's appeal to the nation as saying.
"I am sure everything will go alright," the statement added. "I believe that I will soon be working at full strength, as I did before."
Yeltsin said in September he had agreed to have an operation to improve blood supply to his heart and allow him to live a normal life.
Yastrzhembsky said a team of four surgeons, headed by Russian specialist Renat Akchurin, had started operating at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT). Surgery of this kind usually lasted six to eight hours, he added.

Yastrzhembsky said the president was in jovial mood before the operation, joking with chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov. "Are you here with the knife already?" Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as asking Mironov.
